**4. Matters Arising from the Previous Minutes**

Councillor Ford queried the status of the action item regarding the overgrown hedge at the junction of New Street and The Homend. Councillor Ford asked that the action item be kept open until the works were completed. The Committee agreed.

Ledbury District Council approved the new market square seating plan. Record status: historical.

---

**5. Public Participation**

The Chair invited members of the public to speak on items on the agenda.

**5.1** Mr. A. Tipton spoke in objection to Planning Application 25/0123/F (item 6), relating to the conversion of a barn at Upper Hall Farm, Little Marcle. Mr. Tipton raised concerns about the impact of the proposed conversion on the setting of the Grade II listed barn, and questioned whether the applicant's structural survey was sufficiently detailed. He also noted that the access track was narrow and had no passing places.

**5.2** Mrs. R. Vane spoke in support of Planning Application 25/0145/L (item 8), relating to the change of use of land at the former Hop Kiln, Bosbury. Mrs. Vane stated that the proposed use as a small-scale camping site would bring much-needed tourism income to the parish, and that the applicant had agreed to a condition limiting the number of pitches to twelve.

**5.3** Mr. J. Okafor (no relation to Ms. Okafor) spoke on behalf of the Ledbury Market Square Traders' Association regarding the future of the market square seating plan. Mr. Okafor said that traders had been consulted informally and that there was broad support for replacing the existing benches with movable seating units, but that traders wanted assurance that the new seating would not reduce the space available for market stalls on Saturdays. The Chair thanked Mr. Okafor for his comments and noted that the matter was on the agenda for a future meeting of the Committee, but was not listed for decision at this meeting.

---

**6. Planning Application 25/0123/F – Upper Hall Farm, Little Marcle**

The Committee considered a report by the Head of Planning Services (Report PC/2025/06) regarding a full planning application for the conversion of an agricultural barn to a single dwelling, with associated access and landscaping.

Mr. D. Cole presented the report. He drew the Committee's attention to the key issues, which were: (a) the principle of development in the open countryside; (b) the impact on the setting of the Grade II listed barn; (c) highway safety; and (d) biodiversity net gain. He noted that the application had been recommended for refusal, as the structural survey submitted by the applicant was considered inadequate to demonstrate that the barn was structurally sound and suitable for conversion without substantial rebuilding. The officer recommendation was therefore one of refusal, contrary to the National Planning Policy Framework's presumption in favour of sustainable development.

**7. Ledbury Bus Service Subsidy Review**

The Committee received a report by the Head of Transport (Report TIC/2025/12) on the outcome of the public consultation on the future of the subsidised bus service 445 (Ledbury–Hereford). The report summarised the 312 responses received, of which 78% expressed strong opposition to any reduction in service frequency or withdrawal of the service. Key concerns raised included access to hospital appointments, employment, and the daytime shopping service for elderly and disabled residents.

7.1 The Head of Transport noted that the current subsidy contract was due to expire on 31 October 2025, and that the operator had indicated a willingness to continue providing the service under a revised contract. The report set out three options: (a) maintain the current level of subsidy and frequency; (b) reduce the subsidy by 15% and negotiate a reduced timetable with the operator; or (c) withdraw the subsidy entirely and rely on the commercial market. The report recommended option (b) as a compromise, noting that a 15% reduction would require the service to operate on a reduced timetable, with an hourly frequency rather than the current half-hourly frequency during peak times.

7.2 Councillor Craddock spoke against option (b), stating that the service was a lifeline for many residents in the Ledbury area and that any reduction in frequency would have a significant impact on those who relied on it. She proposed an amendment to the recommendation that the current level of subsidy be maintained for a further 12 months, funded from the Committee's contingency budget.

7.3 The amendment was seconded by Councillor Patel. A debate followed in which members discussed the financial pressures on the Council's transport budget, the importance of maintaining bus services in rural areas, and the need to make savings in the light of the overall budget settlement.

**6. Planning Application 25/0087/F – Land off Little Marcle Road**

6.1 The Principal Planning Officer presented the report on an application for the erection of 12 dwellings with associated access, landscaping and open space. The application had been the subject of a site visit on 27 February 2025.

6.2 The Principal Planning Officer noted that the application had been amended since the site visit to reduce the number of dwellings from 14 to 12 and to revise the layout to provide additional tree planting along the eastern boundary. The amended plans had been re-consulted on, and no further objections had been received from statutory consultees.

6.3 Councillor Osei, having declared an interest, spoke as a member of the Ledbury Civic Trust. He noted that the Trust had submitted a representation objecting to the original scheme on the grounds of the loss of a hedgerow and the impact on the setting of the adjacent listed building. He said that the amended scheme had gone some way to addressing these concerns, but the Trust remained concerned about the impact on the setting of the listed building.

6.4 The Head of Planning confirmed that the amended scheme had been assessed by the Council's Conservation Officer, who had advised that the revised layout, with the additional planting and the repositioning of the access road, would result in a less than substantial harm to the setting of the listed building, and that this harm was outweighed by the public benefits of the scheme, including the provision of affordable housing.

6.5 Councillor Craddock proposed that the application be approved, subject to the conditions set out in the report, with an additional condition requiring the submission of a construction management plan prior to the commencement of any works. The proposal was seconded by Councillor Bains.

6.6 A vote was taken. The motion was carried unanimously.

**RESOLVED: That application 25/0087/F be approved, subject to the conditions set out in the report and the additional condition relating to the construction management plan.**

MA opened the discussion, stating that the town centre redevelopment proposal, submitted by Ledbury Properties Ltd, had been formally validated by Herefordshire Council the previous week. The planning application (Ref. P/2501/045/F) covers the former cattle market site and includes 120 residential units, retail space, and a new public square.

MA stated that this was the most significant local planning story of the year and that the editorial voice of the paper needed to be clear and well-argued. She proposed that she would personally write the lead editorial for the edition of 23 January, timed to coincide with the public consultation deadline.

PROPOSAL: That the editorial for 23 January should address the balance between housing need and preserving the character of Ledbury town centre.

DECISION: The editorial should be supportive of the principle of regeneration but should raise specific concerns about traffic impact and the height of the proposed buildings. The editorial should also call for a transparent consultation process.

3.2 Ms. E. Furlong asked for an update on the progress of the Ross-on-Wye cycle link. The Head of Transport advised that the scheme was in its detailed design stage, with a planning application expected in the autumn. A further report would be brought to the Committee when the design was complete.

**6. Chair's Announcements**

6.1 The Chair welcomed everyone to the meeting and noted that this was the first meeting of the Committee to be held in the newly refurbished Plaughley Hall chamber. He thanked the building services team for their work.

6.2 The Chair reminded members that the deadline for submitting questions for the next meeting was Friday, 14 March 2025.

---

**7. Ledbury Bus Service Subsidy Review**

The Committee received a report by the Head of Transport (Report TIC/2025/12) on the outcome of the public consultation on the future of the subsidised bus service 445 (Ledbury–Hereford). The report summarised the 312 responses received, of which 78% expressed strong opposition to any reduction in service frequency or withdrawal of the service. Key concerns raised included access to hospital appointments, employment, and the daytime shopping service for elderly and disabled residents.

7.1 The Head of Transport noted that the current subsidy contract was due to expire on 31 October 2025, and that the operator had indicated a willingness to continue providing the service under a revised contract. The report set out three options: (a) maintain the current level of subsidy and frequency; (b) reduce the subsidy by 15% and negotiate a reduced timetable with the operator; or (c) withdraw the subsidy entirely and rely on the commercial market. The report recommended option (b) as a compromise, noting that a 15% reduction would require the service to operate on a reduced timetable, with an hourly frequency rather than the current half-hourly frequency during peak times.

7.2 Councillor Craddock spoke against option (b), stating that the service was a lifeline for many residents in the Ledbury area and that any reduction in frequency would have a significant impact on those who relied on it. She proposed an amendment to the recommendation that the current level of subsidy be maintained for a further 12 months, funded from the Committee's contingency budget.

7.3 The amendment was seconded by Councillor Patel. A debate followed in which members discussed the financial pressures on the Council's transport budget, the importance of maintaining bus services in rural areas, and the need to make savings in the light of the overall budget settlement.

The window was proposed to match the style of existing windows on the main house.

Councillor Henshaw asked about parking provision. The Principal Planning Officer confirmed that one off-street parking space would be provided within the curtilage, and that the highway authority had raised no objection.

The Chair invited the applicant's agent, Mr. R. Timms, to speak in support of the application. Mr. Timms stated that the proposal would provide much-needed smaller accommodation in the village and that the works would be carried out using traditional materials to a high standard.

The Committee debated the application. Councillor Fletcher noted that the proposal was modest in scale and would preserve the character of the listed building and its setting. Councillor Whitmore agreed, stating that the change of use would secure the long-term maintenance of the coach house.

Councillor Barnaby moved the recommendation to approve, which was seconded by Councillor Vaughan.

**RESOLVED:** That Application 25/0112/F be approved subject to the conditions set out in the report of the Head of Planning, including conditions relating to the materials to be used and the method of insertion of the north elevation window.
